primary_cross_section_source.citation: John N. Bahcall, Gallium Solar Neutrino Experiments: Absorption Cross Sections, Neutrino Spectra, and Predicted Event Rates, Phys. Rev. C 56, 3391 (1997)
primary_cross_section_source.coverage: 71Ga neutrino-capture best-estimate cross section from 0.240 to 30.000 MeV
primary_cross_section_source.source_instruction: cubic spline fit to tabulated cross sections as a function of energy
primary_cross_section_source.reported_reproduction_scale: 1% or better for standard-spectrum best-estimate cross sections

source_line_source.citation: S. R. Elliott, V. N. Gavrin, and W. C. Haxton, Gallium neutrino absorption cross section and its uncertainty, Phys. Rev. C 108, 035502 (2023)

original_files.role: paper source containing exact line table

production_payloads.role: lossless machine-readable transcription of the Best table
machine-readable transcription of published source lines

cross_section.representation: natural cubic spline in linear energy and linear cross section
cross_section.differentiability: C2 on closed payload domain with one-sided endpoint derivative
cross_section.derivative: analytic derivative of frozen spline polynomials
cross_section.uncertainty_representation: published -3sigma and +3sigma tables preserved in source but not selected as production scenario

license_and_publication_provenance.status: published scientific material; bibliographic attribution required

limitations: The 1997 source specifies cubic splines but not endpoint boundary conditions; natural endpoints are a frozen numerical convention.
The derivative of the interpolant is deterministic but does not have a separately published derivative uncertainty guarantee.
The selected model is one frozen conventional cross-section scenario, not a claim that alternative nuclear calculations are invalid.
